feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 3 (y=0.07 m, 51.31) raised s-bend progress to 0.155 but gave steering_oscillation 0.127 (s-bend) and 0.138 (slalom), with one line loss per run on those tracks. Iteration 4 (y=0.06 m, 36.81) still had oscillation 0.141 on slalom and s-bend line loss of 0.9, and its s-bend progress fell back to 0.0495. So the lead above about 0.06 m is too aggressive for this controller, and the lead gain on bends is partly lost when it is pulled back. The oval is fixed at progress 0.115 and max_error 0.061 m across iterations 1 to 4 whatever sensing, mass or track width was tried, so geometry alone is unlikely to fix it. What I had to compensate for: I held kp 2.0 and kd 0.10 unchanged, because lead changes already moved the signal's timing; I kept ki 0 to avoid windup on bends. Next race: if steering_oscillation is below 0.10 on slalom and s-bend with line_loss_events 0 and the score at or above 51, keep y=0.05 m and test y=0.055 m. If oscillation is still above 0.10 at y=0.05 m, the lead is not the cause, so tell me and I will change wheel_radius to 0.04 m next. If the s-bend progress falls to the 0.04 level, the lead is not helping at this row, so return to y=0.06 m and change nothing else.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation is still above 0.10 on slalom and s-bend at sensor y=0.05 m (iteration 4 gave 0.141 at y=0.06 m), keep the row at y=0.05 m and set wheel_radius to 0.04 m to test whether ground speed, not lead, is the cause.

If the score is above 51.3 with zero line loss on s-bend and slalom (iteration 3 had one loss per run on each), keep y=0.05 m and test y=0.055 m, a midpoint between 0.05 and 0.06 m, changing nothing else.

If s-bend progress falls back to the 0.04 level (iterations 0 to 2 and 4 show about 0.04 to 0.05), the lead is not helping, so return the row to y=0.06 m and change only kd, from 0.10 to 0.15, to damp the jitter at that lead (iteration 4 showed 0.141 oscillation).
